chose: Every tool call is a call line in a replay record of its own, .coherence/replay/<session>.jsonl, beside the read trace's read, write and snapshot lines, which stay as they were for calibrate and the live lighting
over: a call line replacing the read and write lines inside the trace file
because: git keeps or ignores whole files, never some of a file's lines, so the record commitReplay may commit cannot share a file with the stop's snapshots, which are machine-local (inode fingerprints, predicted closures); keeping the trace's lines also leaves calibrate, sessionPatch and TraceTail untouched, at the cost of a read or a write being written twice, one append each
binding: none: this session owns no active work order

chose: A subagent's calls go into its coordinator's replay record (the event's session_id), each line naming the subagent's own session (agent_id) and agent type
over: one replay record per subagent, keyed as the read trace is by the subagent's id
because: the owner asked to see what the agent has been up to: one session's record then holds everything done under it, parallel subagents interleaved by time, and the journal's attribution (session and agent per line) still tells them apart

chose: The config key is commitReplay, false by default; Coherence's .coherence/.gitignore comes in two texts chosen by it, both Coherence's, and .gitattributes always gives replay/ merge=union and linguist-generated whatever the key says
over: commitTraces, which would read as committing the trace and its snapshots; and attributes written only while the key is true
because: the key names what it commits; attributes on an ignored folder change nothing, while writing them always means a branch that turns the key on merges with one that turned it on earlier, and the attributes file never has to switch texts; the default ignore text stays byte for byte what earlier releases wrote, so no adopter's file churns unless they opt in

chose: Where the adopter's ignore files disagree with commitReplay, the session start and hooks --check say so with the rule git names (check-ignore --no-index -v), never editing the file and never failing the check; the not-committed direction is said only when git ignores the read trace but not the replay folder
over: rewriting the adopter's ignore file, failing hooks --check on a mismatch, or saying the replay folder is unignored in a project whose ignore files keep none of Coherence's state out
because: the ignore file is the adopter's and Coherence never writes it; a mismatch is a commit-policy question, not hook drift, so it must not turn a CI check red; and a project that ignores none of .coherence has a larger gap than the replay record's to name

chose: Replay plays from the live server only, through /api/relief/sessions and /api/relief/replay; a snapshot carries no replay record and shows no replay bar
over: embedding recent sessions' records in the snapshot's state
because: a snapshot is a file handed around, and the record holds the commands an agent ran, which commitReplay keeps on the machine by default; embedding it would publish what the config keeps local, and a snapshot's size would grow with every session

chose: While a replay plays, a live touch lights nothing; paused or ended, live touches light again. Pauses between calls are the real gap held between 0.12 s and 2.4 s, divided by the speed (1x to 32x, 4x by default)
over: lighting live and replayed touches together, and playing at real time
because: two sessions glowing on one relief cannot be told apart, and the reader chose to look at the past one; real time would make a session of long thinking unwatchable, while holding the gaps keeps a burst of calls visibly a burst

chose: A git check-ignore of paths named on its command line is not a project-sized spawn; one fed a list with --stdin still is

because: check-ignore of two named paths reads only the ignore files on those paths, a cost that does not grow with the project; the spec model's ignore check (--stdin with every entry) is the one whose cost grows
